name: Definitions
description: What a piece of source declares, read from the syntax tree.

text: Nesting is recovered from where the nodes sit rather than from the
query: a pattern reaches only its direct children, and tree-sitter has
no operator for a deeper one. Two constructs spanning the same lines
therefore answer with no scope, which loses a prefix rather than

scenarios.title: A name carries the scopes holding it
given: a file nesting a module inside a module
scenarios.when: the file is read for what it declares
scenarios.then: each name answers qualified by the scopes it sits in

scenarios.title: A singleton method and an instance one
given: a class declaring one of each
scenarios.when: the file is read for what it declares
scenarios.then: the two are told apart by the way Ruby spells them

scenarios.title: A scope written with its path
given: a module named the way a path is written rather than by nesting
scenarios.when: the file is read for what it declares
scenarios.then: the name answers whole, as the source spelled it

scenarios.title: A definition outside every scope
given: a method declared at the top level of a file
scenarios.when: the file is read for what it declares
scenarios.then: it answers by its bare name, because there is no path to put in front of it

scenarios.title: Source the grammar cannot read
given: a Ruby file the grammar cannot parse
scenarios.when: the file is read for what it declares
scenarios.then: the file is named as unreadable rather than answering with the names it recovered

scenarios.title: A method written inside a reopened singleton class
given: a class whose `class << self` declares a method
scenarios.when: the file is read for what it declares
scenarios.then: the name is spelled as belonging to the class rather than to an instance of it

scenarios.title: The kind of each parameter
given: a method declaring a positional, a keyword, a splat and a block parameter
scenarios.when: the file is read for what it declares
scenarios.then: each parameter answers with the kind Ruby's spelling gives it, in the order the source wrote them

scenarios.title: A parameter a caller may leave out
given: a method declaring a parameter with a default, and one gathering the rest
scenarios.when: the file is read for what it declares
scenarios.then: each of them answers as optional

scenarios.title: A parameter with no name
given: a method declaring an anonymous splat
scenarios.when: the file is read for what it declares
scenarios.then: it answers with its kind and no name

scenarios.title: A method declaring no parameters
given: a method written with an empty parameter list
scenarios.when: the file is read for what it declares
scenarios.then: it answers an empty list of parameters

scenarios.title: A scope takes no parameters at all
scenarios.when: the file is read for what it declares
scenarios.then: it answers no parameters, rather than an empty list of them

scenarios.title: A declaration that names no parameter
scenarios.when: the file is read for what it declares
scenarios.then: the method answers only the parameters it takes

scenarios.title: A method a call brings into being
given: a class whose method is written as `attr_reader`
scenarios.when: the file is read for what it declares
scenarios.then: the method is not among what the file declares

scenarios.title: A method a class mixes in
scenarios.when: the file is read for what it declares
scenarios.then: the class does not declare the method
